root_motivation: The buildloop's deploy gate treats the rollback-plan receipt as a ship blocker. For a crate that ships as a redeployable tagged binary, the receipt asks a question with no bearing on the real rollback path. `autobuilder/src/rollback.rs` resolves a base tag, then sets `verdict = if blocking == 0 { "pass" } else { "block" }` where `blocking` counts commits that are not `git revert`-clean (merge commits always count, `parent_count > 1`). mcphost's history is deliberately interleaved — every parallel-extend integrate since v0.5.5 lands a `--no-ff` merge plus a version bump — so `blocking` is never zero and the receipt is red on every HEAD. The concrete cost: v0.13.2 is built and gate-blocked from the hub right now solely on this receipt (plus an unrelated test defect), and every future version will hit the same wall. The operator's 2026-09-05 decision (fix-forward; rollback unit is the version range you would actually revert; base = the currently-deployed version's tag; the non-revert-c...
user_persona: The autobuilder skill orchestrator (a Claude session) and the human invoking `/autobuilder` from their own project. Both shell out to this binary for the receipt + gate steps that must not live in bash.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a crate configured `rollback_model = redeploy-tag` with a contiguous v-tag lineage from the previous deployed tag to HEAD including `--no-ff` merge commits, When rollback-plan runs, Then verdict is pass and the receipt names the previous tag as rollback_target.
Given a library-crate fixture with no rollback_model set and one non-revert-clean commit, When rollback-plan runs, Then verdict is block, identical to the pre-change golden receipt for that fixture.
Given the same library fixture with all commits revert-clean, When rollback-plan runs, Then verdict is pass, identical to the pre-change golden.
Given `redeploy-tag` mode and a crate with zero tags, When rollback-plan runs, Then verdict is block with reason no-previous-tag.
Given the receipt for a redeploy-tag run, When parsed, Then it carries rollback_model, rollback_target (previous tag + sha), and tag_lineage, and validates as schema v2.
Given a v1 rollback receipt on disk, When `autobuilder gate` reads it, Then it is accepted.
Given a version bump in the range that was never tagged, When rollback-plan runs in redeploy-tag mode, Then verdict is block with reason tag-lineage-gap naming that version.
Given `--explain`, When rollback-plan runs, Then it prints the resolved model, base tag, and rollback target on one line.
Given a config declaring an unknown rollback_model value, When rollback-plan runs, Then it exits non-zero naming the invalid value and writes no receipt.
Given mcphost at a HEAD with interleaved v0.13.1/v0.13.2 merge commits configured redeploy-tag with base v0.13.0, When rollback-plan runs, Then verdict is pass.

scope: Stage 4 risk gate (7 receipts + release receipt)
non_goals: Spawning Claude subagents from the binary itself (that is the orchestrator's job)
Web-service, WASM, or embedded scaffolding (v1 supports cli + lib only)
Auto-applying self-evolution proposals (always gated for user review)
Re-running the underlying audit/test commands inside `gate` (gate only attests; producers own the work)

five_whys_trace.q: Why a Rust companion binary instead of a pure-skill scaffold?
five_whys_trace.a: Shell is too easy to subvert (set -e off, grep eaten, jq missing). The load-bearing parts — metric extraction, digest binding, schema validation — need a typed implementation under tests.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a 7-receipt gate instead of `cargo test && cargo clippy`?
five_whys_trace.a: Each receipt covers a class of failure that the others miss: clippy doesn't see CI status, tests don't see proof-lane routing, and none of them produce an independent-review record. The gate is what makes 'ready' falsifiable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bootstrap autobuilder against itself before running it on other projects?
five_whys_trace.a: If the gate model can't certify the binary that produces gate receipts, it can't be trusted on any other project. The meta-bootstrap is the cheapest adversarial test of the whole pipeline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deny unwrap/expect everywhere in src/ when most of this is glue code?
five_whys_trace.a: Glue code that panics on a missing receipt or malformed JSON destroys the audit trail at exactly the moments the gate matters most. Erroring back to the caller keeps the diagnostic surface alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why digest-bind every receipt instead of trusting file timestamps?
five_whys_trace.a: Timestamps lie under git checkout. A self-binding sha256 lets the gate detect tampering and lets reviewers re-verify by recomputing on the receipt's own contents.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the autobuilder repo's 'project' live for the gate — repo root or autobuilder/ workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Repo root. agent/, scripts/, target/autobuilder/ all sit at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder/. Proof-lanes globs use autobuilder/src/** prefix to match `git diff` output.
